main_issue: The mechanism is internally coherent — source shape (MultipartFile.getOriginalFilename), sink (filesystem path concatenation + write), missing guard (no basename normalization), and safe fix (centralized basename extraction) are all well-aligned. However, the boundary is demonstrated by a single representative case from one product (zdh_web), which limits confidence in cross-project generalizability. The reviewer notes correctly distinguish this from static-resource path traversal and archive traversal.

Well-defined boundary row. The mechanism (unbounded file upload causing storage exhaustion) is coherent: source shape (FileStorage.saveStream writing InputStream to FileDescriptor), sink (disk consumption), missing guard (no max bytes before IOUtils.copyLarge), exploit precondition (large upload exhausts disk), and safe fix (configured max, truncate, delete partial, error) are all internally consistent. Pre-patch and post-patch evidence from commit diffs confirms the mechanism is about upload size, not path containment. The mark_out_of_scope decision is sound — this should not be counted as path traversal recall.

Single representative case limits coverage confidence, but the mechanism is narrow, well-defined, and thoroughly evidenced: source shape (FilesResource.updateFile dispatching copy/move), sink (Selectors.SELECT_ALL recursive copy into descendant path), missing guard (no ancestor check before moveTo/copyFrom), exploit precondition (authenticated user places parent into child), and safe fix (checkSourceIsNotParent walking getParent() upward) are all coherent and derived from the same codebase. The guideline text is specific enough to generalize to other systems with recursive copy/move APIs lacking ancestor guards.

The two cases share the same mechanism core: an HTTP request path enters a static-resource resolver, the path is decoded/transformed, and the resolved resource is served without verifying containment within the intended root. Implementation details differ (OpenHAB uses java.io.File canonicalization; Solon uses string prefix matching and repository.find), but the semantic mechanism is coherent. The reviewer notes appropriately scope to static-resource request path resolution, excluding upload filename traversal, archive extraction, and recursive copy/move patterns.
